condition: high-velocity metallic ocular foreign body embedded in the right eye of a machinist
level_rationale: A high-velocity steel sliver embedded in the right eye 15 minutes ago in a machinist carries high risk of open-globe penetration, intraocular metallic foreign body, and infectious endophthalmitis requiring immediate emergency department slit-lamp examination, orbital computed tomography, and emergent ophthalmic intervention, whereas mild dryness in the right eye at quitting time after a 10-hour workday leaves zero traumatic or visual red flags and is appropriate for home self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (34-year-old machinist, working 10 hours today, and a fast-moving steel sliver embedding in the right eye 15 minutes ago) with an exact 7-word vs 7-word span swap and 14 shared trailing tokens. Keeping 'in my right eye' identical across base and control adds zero unstated anatomical structures and leaves zero stranded metal-strike trauma when f3 shifts under Rule A and Rule D to mild right-eye dryness at quitting time after a 10-hour workday (level 4 ER to level 1 home self-care) with zero stated negatives.
